-- Function: create_default_hierarchy(family_id)
-- Idempotent seed of Importance areas + Groupings, then maps the default
-- categories into Groupings by name. Categories whose names aren't in the map
-- (custom or renamed) stay group_id NULL and surface as Uncategorized.
--
-- Called for every existing family below, and by the app (rpc) for new families.
-- ============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id UUID)
RETURNS VOID AS $$
DECLARE
  ess UUID;
  pri UUID;
  oth UUID;
BEGIN
  -- When invoked with an auth context (rpc), only seed the caller's own family.
  -- The migration's DO-loop runs as postgres (auth.uid() IS NULL) and proceeds.
  IF auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.family_members fm
    WHERE fm.family_id = p_family_id
      AND fm.user_id = auth.uid()
      AND fm.status = 'active'
  ) THEN
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  -- Idempotent: bail if this family already has any importance areas.

# YFL Family Expense Tracker

A browser-first expense tracking and reconciliation app for a family: scan receipts,
import bank/credit-card statements, match the two, and report on spending.

Built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5 (runes), Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage), Tailwind CSS 4,
and Mistral Vision for OCR.

## Quick start

Needs **Node 24 or newer** and [OrbStack](https://orbstack.dev) (`brew install --cask orbstack`,
then **launch it once** — see [Local development](#local-development)).

`package.json` sets `engines.node` to `>=24` — a **floor, not a pin**. Running ahead locally is
fine and intended. Note that `.npmrc` sets `engine-strict=true`, so anything below 24 **fails**
`npm install` with `EBADENGINE` rather than warning.

Vercel offers only majors 20/22/24, and resolves the `>=24` range to the newest it has, so
**production builds on 24** while you may be on 26+. The build gate (see
[ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md)) runs on 24 too,
so anything relying on a newer-than-24 API fails the build rather than reaching production.

```bash
npm install
npm run db:up      # start the local Supabase stack
npm run seed:demo  # populate it — prints a login and password
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173
```

## Commands

Every command in the project, in one place. Everything defaults to the **local** Supabase stack;
only the explicit `:remote` variant talks to **production**.

```bash
# ── Run the app ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
npm run dev                    # Dev server → local Supabase stack
npm run dev:remote             # Dev server → PRODUCTION (needs 1Password `op`)
npm run build                  # Production build
npm run preview                # Serve the production build locally

# ── Local database (Supabase stack; needs OrbStack running) ───────────────────
npm run db:up                  # Start the stack
npm run db:down                # Stop it
npm run db:reset               # Drop + rebuild the DB from the baseline migration
npm run db:studio              # Open Supabase Studio (http://127.0.0.1:54323)

# ── Demo data (local only) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
npm run seed:demo              # Seed the demo family
npm run seed:demo:teardown     # Remove it (or just `npm run db:reset`)

# ── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
npm test                       # Full suite: unit + e2e
npm run test:unit              # Vitest, single run (browser + node projects)
npm run test:watch             # …in watch mode — the fast inner loop
npm run test:e2e               # Playwright e2e (add `-- --ui` for the UI runner)
npm run test:integration       # RLS tests against the local stack (needs db:up)

# ── Quality gates ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
npm run verify                 # THE ONE TO RUN before pushing — see below

I have a thorough picture. Here is the map.

## 1. Tech stack & architecture

**Stack** (from `README.md`, `package.json`): SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 (runes), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, deployed on Vercel. Backend is **Supabase** (Postgres + Auth + Storage) plus **Supabase Edge Functions** (Deno, in `supabase/functions/`). Charts use `layerchart`; spreadsheet import via `xlsx`; PDF export via `pdf-lib`.

**Is there a backend?** Yes, but thin. It is a browser-first SPA that talks directly to Supabase from the client (`src/lib/supabaseClient.ts`, using `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` / `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`). Server-side code is limited to two SvelteKit API routes for OCR (`src/routes/api/ocr/+server.ts`, `src/routes/api/ocr/extract/+server.ts`) and Deno edge functions for inbound-email receipt parsing (`supabase/functions/`).

**Where expense data lives:** Postgres tables in Supabase (not local files or browser storage). Key tables (from `src/lib/services/*` and `supabase/migrations/20260726120000_baseline.sql`): `receipts`, `expense_categories` (receipt→category join, 1:1), `categories`, `category_groups`, `importance_areas`, `transactions`, `families`, `family_members`, `profiles`. Data is **family-scoped** (`family_id`) and guarded by RLS. Receipt images live in Supabase Storage. There is no per-user local persistence.

## 2. The Spending tab

- Route/UI: `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` (year selection lives in the URL via `src/routes/spending/+page.ts` → `?year=`). There is also `src/routes/spending/hierarchy/+page.svelte` for editing the hierarchy.
- All aggregation is one pure function: **`buildSpendingReport()` in `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts`**. The page only loads data and paints the grid.
- It rolls a year's expenses up through **Category → Grouping (CategoryGroup) → Area of Importance**, producing a month-by-month grid: columns run January → the last month with any expense, plus a Year-to-Date column, an Uncategorized section, and a Grand Total. Amounts are normalized to CAD via `total_amount * (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`; refunds stay negative so they net out. Rows with zero activity are suppressed.
- Related utilities: `spendingComparison.ts` (year-over-year prior-period totals), `spendingDrilldown.ts` (builds `/expenses?…` filter links from a cell), `spendingChart.ts` + `SpendingChart.svelte` (chart view), `spendingReport.ts` (the aggregation), `spendingYear.ts` (URL year parsing).

## 3. Data shape for category-by-month totals

The core shapes are exported from `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts`:

```ts
interface SpendingExpense {        // the input rows it consumes
  total_amount: number | null;
  transaction_date: string;        // 'YYYY-MM-DD', bucketed by purchase date
  category_id: string | null;
  exchange_rate_to_cad: number | null;
}
interface Cell { amount: number; count: number; }   // blank when count===0
interface ReportRow {
  name: string;
  categoryId?: string;
  cells: Cell[];        // one per visible month, parallel to SpendingReport.months
  ytd: Cell;
  priorYtd?: number;    // same-period prior-year, attached for comparison
}
interface SpendingReport {
  year: number;
  months: number[];             // 1-based, e.g. [1,2,3,4,5,6]
  monthLabels: string[];        // ['Jan','Feb',...]
  importances: ImportanceSection[];   // each has groups: GroupSection[] + subtotal
  uncategorized: GroupSection | null;
  grandTotal: ReportRow;
  missingAmountCount: number;
}
```

`ImportanceSection` → `GroupSection[]` (each `{name, id?, rows: ReportRow[], subtotal}`) → `ReportRow[]`. This is the natural category-by-month aggregate.

## 4. Categories

The full expense-category list is the `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` constant in **`src/lib/services/CategoryService.ts`** (lines 53–100): Alcohol, Kids - Allowance, Kids - Activities, Banking and Tracking Fees, Birthday Expenses, Car - Other Expenses, Car - Repairs & Maintenance, Car - Insurance, Car - Gas, Car - Parking, Clothes, Coffee and Tea, Credit Card Fees, Dental, Donation, Entertainment, Garden, Gifts, Groceries, House Insurance, House Maintenance and Repairs, Household goods, Income taxes, Investments, Meals and Drinks Out, Mortgage, Personal Care, Pharmacy and Medical Tax Deductible, Therapy Tax Deductible (…), Therapy Not Tax Deductible (…), Postage and shipping costs, Property Taxes, Renovation Expenses, Rental Properties, School fees (including Tutors), Sports and Fitness, Travel - Accommodations, Travel - Airfare, Travel - Entertainment, Travel - Food, Travel - Transportation, University expenses, Utilities. These are per-family rows in the `categories` table; families can add/rename/delete their own.

**Yes, there is an existing grouping — a two-tier hierarchy.** Defined by the SQL function `create_default_hierarchy()` in `supabase/migrations-archive/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` (also in the baseline migration). Types are in **`src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts`** (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`).

- **Areas of Importance** (top tier, `sort_order`): **Essential (1), Priorities (2), Other (3)**.
- **Groupings** (middle tier) mapped to areas:
  - Essential: Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes
  - Priorities: Banking & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental
  - Other: Discretionary, Gifts, Travel
- Categories link to a Grouping via `categories.group_id` (null = Uncategorized). Importance attaches to the Grouping, not the individual category. The seed maps default (and legacy spreadsheet) category names into these groupings by name.

So the naming is Essential/Priorities/Other rather than Essential/Important/Discretionary, but the intent is the same — and "Discretionary" exists as a Grouping under "Other."

## 5. Existing AI/GenAI integration

The **only** LLM integration is **Mistral Vision**, used purely for OCR/receipt extraction — not for analysis or insights:
- `supabase/functions/_shared/mistral.ts` — `ocrFromUrl()` and `processEmailText()`, calling `https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions` with model `pixtral-12b-2409`, JSON-object response, keyed by `MISTRAL_API_KEY` (env; also `.env` / 1Password `op`, and `@mistralai/mistralai` SDK is a dependency).
- Client-side wrapper: `src/lib/services/OcrService.ts`; server route `src/routes/api/ocr/extract/+server.ts`; edge function for emailed receipts under `supabase/functions/`.

**No Anthropic/OpenAI/Claude integration anywhere.** No "insights", "analysis", "advice", or "recommendations" feature exists — grep for those terms only hits documentation prose, not code. This is a greenfield opportunity: there is currently no GenAI touchpoint on the Spending data.

## 6. Data export / aggregation utilities (the natural model feed)

- **`buildSpendingReport()` in `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts`** is the ready-made category-by-month aggregate (structured object, exactly what you'd serialize to feed a model).
- `src/lib/services/CSVExportService.ts` — exports a flat expense list to CSV (columns: Date, Merchant Name, Amount, Category). Row-level, not aggregated.
- `src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts` — PDF export of expenses.
- `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` (year-over-year deltas) and `src/lib/utils/spendingDrilldown.ts` (aggregate → filtered expense queries) are supporting aggregation utilities.

The cleanest feed into an LLM is the `SpendingReport` object (or a flattened category×month array derived from `report.importances[].groups[].rows[].cells`), since it already carries CAD-normalized monthly totals, YTD, subtotals per Grouping/Importance, and the Uncategorized bucket.

## 7. User goals / budgets / preferences

**None exist.** There is no budget, goal, target, or user-preference concept in the schema, services, or types (the `budget`/`goal` grep hits are unrelated — image-resize specs and receipt-note code). User-adjustable state is limited to: profile info (`profiles`, additional emails — `src/lib/utils/profileEmails.ts`), family membership, and the customizable category hierarchy itself (categories, groupings, importance areas via the hierarchy editor). Any notion of budgets/goals to compare spending against would be net-new.
